questions.question: Addition to the stock of capital of a firm is known as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Investment**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The addition to a firm's capital stock is known as an investment.
 
• Investment is the process of purchasing assets to generate income or appreciation in the future.
 
• It can also be referred to as capital formation. 
 
• Investment is a broader concept than capital formation, which is the accounting value of new non-financial assets added to the capital stock.
 
• Investment can include all types of capital assets, such as physical property or financial assets. 
 
• Investing is the act of allocating resources, usually capital, with the expectation of generating an income, profit, or gains. Investors typically consider that a greater period of time, like months or years, is needed to generate acceptable returns. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Accumulation
 
 
• Accumulation refers to the process of gathering or increasing resources, assets, or wealth over time. It can apply to financial savings, investments, or even physical goods.
 
• In Economics: It is often associated with the gradual build-up of capital or wealth through saving and reinvesting profits.
 
• Example: A person saving money in a bank account over several years is an example of wealth accumulation.
 
 
 
• Capital Loss
 
 
• A capital loss occurs when the value of an asset decreases, and it is sold for less than its original purchase price.
 
• In Economics/Finance: It is the opposite of a capital gain and often impacts a firm's or individual's financial health negatively.
 
• Example: Selling a property for ₹8 lakh when it was purchased for ₹10 lakh results in a ₹2 lakh capital loss.
 
 
 
• Capital Gain
 
 
• A capital gain occurs when an asset increases in value and is sold for more than its original purchase price.
 
• In Economics/Finance: Capital gains are often taxable and are a common source of income for investors.
 
• Example: Selling stocks for ₹5 lakh that were purchased for ₹3 lakh results in a ₹2 lakh capital gain.

options.text: There no changes in the tastes and preferences of consumers.

questions.solution:

• It considers that the taste, preference, habit, fashion, etc., of the consumer, should remain unchanged.
 
• There should not come a change in the mood of a consumer to try different products.
 
• It is assumed because it breaks the functionality or validity of the law of demand.
 
 
 
• **The income of consumers remains constant:**
 
 
• It considers that the income of the consumer should not change i.e. neither rise nor fall.
 
• It should remain constant because its rise may attract the consumer to buy more goods and raise demand despite an increase in the commodity prices.
 
 
 
• **No changes in the price of substitute goods:**
 
 
• It considers that the price of substitute goods doesn't change and remains the same.
 
• It is assumed so, since, a change in consumer's choice makes the law of demand stand invalid and inapplicable.

questions.question:
What happens in case of market equilibrium:

(a) Market demand = market supply

(b) There is no excess supply in the market
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (a) and (b).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The market attains equilibrium when the market supply and market demand of a commodity become equal.
 
• The term supply refers to how much of a certain product, item, commodity, or service suppliers are willing to make available at a particular price
 
• Demand refers to how much of that product, item, commodity, or service consumers are willing and able to purchase at a particular price
 
• Supply and demand are economic forces of the free market that control what suppliers are willing to produce and what consumers are willing and able to purchase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the market price is above the equilibrium value, there is an excess supply in the market (a surplus), which means there is more supply than demand.
 
• If the market price is below the equilibrium value, then there is an excess in demand (supply shortage).

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII)?

options.text: To design a graphical user interface for operating systems
To enable secure encryption of data for internet transmission
To create a programming language for text-based applications
To define a standardised set of codes for representing text and control characters

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To define a standardised set of codes for representing text and control characters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange)** is a character encoding standard used to represent text in computers, telecommunications, and other devices.
 
• Developed in the **1960s**, ASCII assigns a unique numerical value (0-127) to **letters, digits, punctuation marks, and control characters**.
 
• It enables universal **data exchange between different types of devices and software** by standardizing text representation.
 
• The ASCII standard includes **128 characters**, with codes 0-31 reserved for control characters (e.g., newline, tab) and codes 32-127 for printable characters.
 
• ASCII remains the foundation for many modern encoding systems, including **UTF-8 and Unicode**, which build upon it for broader character support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Character Encoding:** Character encoding is the process of assigning a numerical value to each character, enabling computers to store and manipulate text.
 
• **Control Characters:** ASCII codes 0-31 are reserved for non-printable control characters, such as **newline (code 10)** and **tab (code 9)**.
 
• **Extended ASCII:** Extended ASCII expands the standard 128 characters to include 256 characters, incorporating additional symbols, accents, and graphical elements.
 
• **Unicode:** Unicode is a universal character encoding system that supports over 140,000 characters across multiple languages and scripts, building upon ASCII for broader compatibility.
 
• **Usage in Computing:** ASCII codes are widely used in programming, data transfer, and storage to ensure compatibility across systems.

questions.question: When was the first economic census conducted in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1977**__.

__
 
• In 1976, the Government of India launched a planning scheme called **Economic Census and Surveys**.
 
• In 1977**,** Central Statistical Organization conducted the first economic census in collaboration with the Directorate of Economics & Statistics (DES) in the States/Union Territories. 
 
• Economic Census has been conducted earlier throughout the country during the years 1977,1980,1990, 1998, and 2005,2013, and now in 2019.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• All entrepreneurial units in the country which are involved in any economic activities of either agricultural or non-agricultural sector are engaged in production and/or distribution of goods and/or services, not for the sole purpose of own consumption.
 
• It provides detailed information on operational and other characteristics such as the number of establishments, number of persons employed, source of finance, type of ownership, etc.
 
• This information used for micro-level/ decentralized planning and to assess the contribution of various sectors of the economy to the** gross domestic product (GDP).**
 
• **Total Six Economic Censuses (EC) have been conducted to date.**
 
• **The seventh economic census has started in 2019 but due to pandemic and lockdown, it has been extended.**

questions.question: Which command in Windows 10 CMD will delete all .log files in the current directory without asking for confirmation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**del *.log /q**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **del *.log /q** is a Windows CMD command used to delete all **.log files** in the current directory without prompting for confirmation.
 
• The **/q** switch in the command stands for "quiet mode," which suppresses the confirmation prompt.
 
• This command ensures efficient deletion of multiple files in a batch without any manual interruptions.
 
• It is especially useful in scenarios where logs accumulate over time and need regular cleanup.
 
• Using this command requires caution as it deletes files permanently without asking for confirmation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **del Command**

 
 
• The **del** command in Windows CMD is used to delete one or more files.
 
• It does not delete directories; for directories, the **rmdir** command is used.
 
• Using the **/p** switch prompts confirmation before each file deletion.
 
• Wildcard characters like ***** and **?** can be used to specify multiple files.
 
 
 
• **erase Command**
 
 
• The **erase** command is an alias for the **del** command in Windows CMD.
 
• It functions identically to **del** and can be used interchangeably.
 
 
 
• **File Extensions**
 
 
• A file extension like **.log** identifies the type of file, typically used for storing logs or event records.
 
• Log files are often created automatically by software or operating systems to track activities and errors.
 
 
 
• **Precautions When Using CMD Commands**
 
 
• Commands like **del *.log /q** should be used carefully to avoid accidental data loss.
 
• Always verify the directory and file patterns before executing such commands.
 
• Consider creating backups of important files before running deletion commands.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases has Chile recently become the first country in the Americas to be officially verified by the WHO for eliminating as a public health problem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leprosy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **In 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) announced that Chile is the first country in the Americas to achieve the elimination of leprosy as a public health problem.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chile is only the 4th country globally to receive this specific official WHO verification for leprosy elimination.**
 
• The elimination status is defined as reaching a prevalence rate of **less than 1 case per 10,000 population** at the national level.
 
• Key factors for this success included high **Multidrug Therapy (MDT)** coverage and effective prevention of physical disabilities.
 
• The country maintained a high treatment completion rate of over **95%** and a very low proportion of cases among children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Leprosy (Hansen’s Disease)__

 __
 
• Causative Agent - A slow-growing bacterium called ***Mycobacterium leprae***.
 
• Impact - It primarily affects the skin, nerves, upper respiratory tract, and eyes. If left untreated, it can cause permanent damage.
 
 
 
• Global Leprosy Strategy__
 __
 
• Goal - The WHO's Global Leprosy Strategy (2021–2030) aims for "Towards Zero Leprosy," focusing on zero infection, zero disease, and zero stigma.
 
 
 
• Multidrug Therapy (MDT)__
 
 
• Nature - A combination of three antibiotics (Dapsone, Rifampicin, and Clofazimine) which has been the gold standard for curing leprosy since the 1980s.

questions.question: _________ are often referred to as the amphibians of the plant kingdom.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **1** i.e __**Bryophyta**__.

**Explanation:**

 
• Bryophytes are often referred to as the amphibians of the plant kingdom.
 
• Bryophytes are small, non-vascular plants.
 
• The reproduction of Bryophytes is via **spores**.
 
• Bryophytes live in the soil, even though they need water for **sexual reproduction** this is the **reason why the Bryophytes are often referred to as the amphibians of the plant kingdom.**
 
• Bryophytes are generally classified into three coordinate phyla namely **the liverworts, hornworts, and mosses.**

 
 

 Phanerogamae 
 
 
 
• Plants that have seeds are called Phanerogamae.
 
• Also called **Spermatophytes**.
 
• Classified into two: Gymnosperms (naked seed plants) and Angiosperms (covered seed plants).
 
 
 
 

 Pteridophyta
 
 
 
• Vascular plant that disperses spores.
 
• Reproduce by releasing spores rather than seeds.
 
 
 
 

 Thallophyta
 
 
 
• Thallophyta included the algae, bacteria, fungi, and lichens.
 
• Autotrophic in nature.
 
• The reproductive system is hidden.
